symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the propensity score.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the control regression.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the continuous conditional-effect version.

symbols.name: c_0
symbols.def: A fixed numerical upper bound on expected occupancy of one core cell.

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: Number of public microcells, with \(k\asymp h^d/\ell^d\).

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: Common probability and volume of a core cell, with \(v\asymp\ell^d\).

symbols.name: pi
symbols.def: The continuous Hölder version of \(P(A=1\mid X=x)\) when that version exists.

symbols.name: mu_0
symbols.def: The continuous Hölder version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=x]\) when that version exists.

symbols.name: mu_1
symbols.def: A measurable version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=x]\).

symbols.name: tau
symbols.def: The unique continuous Hölder representative of the \(P_X\)-almost-everywhere class \(\mu_1-\mu_0\) when such a representative exists.

symbols.name: sim_1
symbols.def: \(D_n\sim_1D_n'\) when the ordered datasets differ in at most one record by replacement.

symbols.name: R_NP
symbols.def: Nonprivate minimax absolute risk for \(\theta(P)\) over \(\mathcal M_H\).

symbols.name: T_DP
symbols.def: A generic pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially private estimator under replacement adjacency.

symbols.name: R_DP
symbols.def: Pure-private minimax absolute risk for \(\theta(P)\) over \(\mathcal M_H\).

symbols.name: C_j
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th disjoint public core cube, \(j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), of volume \(v\).

symbols.name: zeta_h
symbols.def: A public macro cutoff supported in \(Q_h\) and equal to one at \(x_0\) and on every \(C_j\).

symbols.name: psi_j
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th public scale-\(\ell\) profile, equal to one on \(C_j\), with fixed bounded overlap and \(\sum_{j=1}^k\psi_j(x)^2=1\) on \(\operatorname{supp}(\zeta_h)\).

symbols.name: xi
symbols.def: Scalar nuisance sign for the constant-mixture obstruction.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Propensity perturbation amplitude calibrated at order \(\ell^\alpha\).

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: Outcome perturbation amplitude calibrated at order \(\ell^\beta\).

symbols.name: P_s_lambda
symbols.def: The smooth binary-outcome component law indexed by \((s,\lambda)\).

symbols.name: P_const_xi
symbols.def: The constant-effect-zero component law indexed by \(\xi\).

symbols.name: Q_const
symbols.def: The causal law whose observed-data marginal is \((P_{\mathrm{const},-}+P_{\mathrm{const},+})/2\).

symbols.name: phi_pair
symbols.def: \(\phi_{\mathrm{pair}}(D_n)=\operatorname{sign}\{S_{\mathrm{pair}}(D_n)+W\}\), with an independent fair tie-break at zero.

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: Public core-cell label in the quantized diagnostic experiment.

symbols.name: q_core
symbols.type: Map from the binary core-record space to \(\mathcal Z_k\)

symbols.name: sigma_quant
symbols.def: \(\sigma_{2,k}=1\) if \(T_{2,k}>0\), \(\sigma_{2,k}=-1\) if \(T_{2,k}<0\), and \(\sigma_{2,k}\) is an independent fair Rademacher variable if \(T_{2,k}=0\).

symbols.name: sim_quant
symbols.def: \((z_1,z_2)\sim_{\mathrm q}(z_1',z_2')\) when at most one complete quantized record is replaced.

symbols.name: RR_quant
symbols.def: Conditional on \(\sigma_{2,k}\), report \(\sigma_{2,k}\) with probability \(e^\epsilon/(1+e^\epsilon)\) and report \(-\sigma_{2,k}\) otherwise.

symbols.name: r_pair
symbols.role: nonprivate separation scale of the signed pair experiment

symbols.name: t_P
symbols.def: \(t_P\) is the smallest grid point minimizing \(d_\Theta(t,\theta(P))\).

symbols.name: Q_score
symbols.type: Family of measurable maps \(Q_t:\mathcal O^n\to\mathbb R\), indexed by \(t\in\mathcal G_r\)
symbols.def: A target-indexed score family to be derived by the full-fiber lifting question.

symbols.name: T_shell
symbols.type: Markov kernel from \(\mathcal O^n\) to \(\mathcal G_r\)

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: Scalar threshold indexing separated target fibers.

symbols.name: H_pair_lift
symbols.def: A second-order least-favorable-mixture, Hoeffding-projection, and occupancy-normalization handle for constructing the full score family \(Q_t\).

standard.name: Interior-point specialization of the pointwise Hölder model

novel.justification: The strict ordering \(q<\gamma\) is a two-scale geometric restriction: nuisance profiles may vary on microcells of scale \(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\) inside a target-effect region of scale \(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\), so \(\ell<h\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). It holds, for example, in the finite audit with \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), and \(\gamma=1\), and describes settings in which the causal effect is smoother than the combined propensity and control nuisances.

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the observed-data marginal induced by \(P\).

novel.justification: Known exact uniformity describes benchmark studies in which covariate locations are publicly generated while treatment assignment remains observational with an unknown propensity score.
This pure-central regime contains fixed privacy budgets and budgets decreasing to the saturation boundary \(n^{-1}\), including the range in which a nonconstant pair release is informative.

definitions.name: Exact-uniform coupled-nuisance Hölder class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_H=\{P:P\text{ is a law on }(Y_0,Y_1,A,X)\text{ inducing }O\in\mathcal O\text{ and satisfying }\text{ass:dimension},\text{ass:interior-point},\text{ass:consistency},\text{ass:exchangeability},\text{ass:uniform-design},\text{ass:overlap},\text{ass:propensity-holder},\text{ass:control-holder},\text{ass:effect-holder},\text{ass:two-scale-geometry}\}\), indexed by \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,q,L,e_0,x_0\).

definitions.name: Pure-private minimax risk
definitions.construction: \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}=\inf_{T_{\mathrm{DP}}:\,\epsilon\text{-DP}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n},T_{\mathrm{DP}}}|T_{\mathrm{DP}}(D_n)-\theta(P)|\), with privacy required on all of \(\mathcal O^n\) under \(\sim_1\).

definitions.name: Two-resolution smooth profile system
definitions.construction: Choose fixed compactly supported \(C^\infty\) bumps so that \(Q_h\) contains \(k\asymp h^d/\ell^d\) disjoint core cubes \(C_j\) of volume \(v\asymp\ell^d\); \(\zeta_h=1\) at \(x_0\) and on their union; \(\psi_j=1\) on \(C_j\); the profile supports have fixed bounded overlap; and \(\sum_{j=1}^k\psi_j^2=1\) on \(\operatorname{supp}(\zeta_h)\).

definitions.name: Smooth signed two-fiber CATE family
definitions.construction: Let \(F_\lambda=\zeta_h\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j\psi_j\), \(K_h=\mathbb E_\lambda F_\lambda^2=\zeta_h^2\), and \(D_{\mathrm{fuz}}=1/4-a^2K_h\). Define \(\pi_\lambda=1/2+aF_\lambda\), \(m_{s,\lambda}=1/2+sbF_\lambda\), \(\tau_s=-sabK_h/D_{\mathrm{fuz}}\), \(\mu_{0,s,\lambda}=m_{s,\lambda}-\pi_\lambda\tau_s\), and \(\mu_{1,s,\lambda}=m_{s,\lambda}+(1-\pi_\lambda)\tau_s\). Under \(P_{s,\lambda}\), draw \(X\) uniformly, draw independent binary potential outcomes conditional on \(X\) with means \(\mu_{0,s,\lambda}(X)\) and \(\mu_{1,s,\lambda}(X)\), draw \(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_\lambda(X))\) independently of the potential outcomes, and set \(Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\).

definitions.name: Constant convex-hull witness
definitions.construction: Under \(P_{\mathrm{const},\xi}\), let \(X\) be uniform, set \(P(A=1\mid X)=1/2+a\xi\), and draw independent binary potential outcomes with common mean \(1/2+b\xi\), independently of \(A\) conditional on \(X\). Let \(Q_{\mathrm{const}}\) have observed-data marginal \((P_{\mathrm{const},-}+P_{\mathrm{const},+})/2\) and a causal realization with its induced constant arm means.

definitions.name: Shared nuisance-sign sample mixtures
definitions.construction: \(\Pi_s^n=2^{-k}\sum_{\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^k}P_{s,\lambda}^{\otimes n}\) for \(s\in\{-1,1\}\); one common \(\lambda\) is retained across all records within each product law.

definitions.name: Occupancy-normalized pair score
definitions.construction: Set \(U_i=2A_i-1\), \(V_i=2Y_i-1\), and \(Z_{ir}=(U_iV_r+V_iU_r)/2\). For each public core \(C_j\), let \(B_j=0\) when \(N_j<2\), and otherwise let \(B_j=\{N_j(N_j-1)\}^{-1}\sum_{i\ne r:X_i,X_r\in C_j}Z_{ir}\). Define \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}=\sum_{j=1}^kB_j\).

definitions.name: Pure-private pair test and estimator
definitions.construction: Compute \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}(D_n)\), draw \(W\sim\operatorname{Laplace}(4/\epsilon)\), return the sign with an independent fair tie-break, and set \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{pair}}=-\phi_{\mathrm{pair}}ab/(1/4-a^2)\).

definitions.name: Fully specified quantized core experiment
definitions.construction: Restrict a binary component record to \(X\in\bigcup_{j=1}^kC_j\) and apply \(q_{\mathrm{core}}(Y,A,X)=(j,2A-1,2Y-1)\). Equivalently, conditional on \((s,\lambda)\), draw \(J\) uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and then draw \((U,V)\) with \(Q_{s,\lambda}^{(k)}\{(j,u,w)\}=(4k)^{-1}(1+2a\lambda_ju+2sb\lambda_jw)\). For two records retain the same \(\lambda\) and average it uniformly to obtain \(\overline\Pi_{s,k}^{\,2}\). The sample space is \(\mathcal Z_k^2\), the collision event is \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{coll}}=\{J_1=J_2\}\), and replacement adjacency is \(\sim_{\mathrm q}\).

definitions.name: Quantized randomized-response channel
definitions.construction: Compute \(T_{2,k}=\mathbf 1\{\mathcal E_{\mathrm{coll}}\}(U_1V_2+V_1U_2)/2\); set \(\sigma_{2,k}\) to its sign, using an independent fair Rademacher tie-break when \(T_{2,k}=0\); report \(RR_{2,k}=\sigma_{2,k}\) with probability \(e^\epsilon/(1+e^\epsilon)\) and its negative otherwise; and set \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{RR}}=-RR_{2,k}ab/(1/4-a^2)\).

definitions.name: Target metric and scalar shells
definitions.construction: Use \(d_\Theta(t,t')=|t-t'|\), the ordered grid \(\mathcal G_r\), the lower-tie nearest point \(t_P\), and shells \(\mathcal S_m(P;r)=\{t\in\mathcal G_r:mr\le d_\Theta(t,t_P)<(m+1)r\}\).

definitions.name: Second-order full-fiber lifting handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(H_{\mathrm{pair\mbox{-}lift}}\): solve each finite minimax threshold problem between \(\mathcal F_-(u,\delta)\) and \(\mathcal F_+(u,\delta)\); retain its sample-level least-favorable mixture; extract and localize the first nonzero second-order Hoeffding projection into public microcells; normalize occupied cells by realized ordered-pair counts as in \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}\); stabilize only the residual higher-order term; and aggregate the resulting target-indexed scores through \(\mathfrak W_r\).

statements.statement: Consistency, armwise conditional exchangeability, and overlap imply that \(\mu_a\) is a version of \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X=x]\) for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\). Under the known uniform design and Hölder effect condition, \(\tau\) is the unique continuous representative of the almost-everywhere conditional causal contrast \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x]\). Hence \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(x_0)\) is identified as the value at \(x_0\) of that continuous representative.
statements.justification: The continuous-version convention makes pointwise CATE identification well posed under a continuous design.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. use the same causal model; this lemma makes explicit the continuous representative required at a probability-zero covariate point.
statements.consumer: It permits every testing separation below to be interpreted as a separation of identified pointwise causal effects.

statements.statement: There are positive constants depending only on \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\) such that, whenever \(a\le c\ell^\alpha\), \(b\le c\ell^\beta\), and \(ab\le ch^\gamma\), every \(P_{s,\lambda}\), every \(P_{\mathrm{const},\xi}\), and \(Q_{\mathrm{const}}\) belong to \(\mathcal M_H\). Moreover, \(\theta(P_{s,\lambda})=-sab/(1/4-a^2)\), \(\theta(P_{\mathrm{const},\xi})=0\), and \(\theta(Q_{\mathrm{const}})=4ab\).
statements.justification: The obstruction and pair test are relevant only when every component and mixture law remains in the unchanged destination class.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. prove localized fuzzy-family membership for a nonprivate lower bound; this statement adds exact shared-sign and constant convex-hull algebra tailored to a private upper test.
statements.consumer: It makes both finite obstructions and the pair-test guarantee same-class statements.

statements.statement: The constant witness satisfies \((P_{\mathrm{const},-}+P_{\mathrm{const},+})/2=Q_{\mathrm{const}}\) on the observed one-record experiment, although the two component laws have target zero and \(Q_{\mathrm{const}}\) has target \(4ab\). The signed family also satisfies \(2^{-k}\sum_\lambda P_{+,\lambda}=2^{-k}\sum_\lambda P_{-,\lambda}\) on one observed record. Consequently, the relevant target fibers have intersecting one-record convex hulls, and every bounded additive one-record score has zero prior-averaged expectation margin for the signed pair of fibers.
statements.justification: This establishes on legal unknown-propensity CATE laws that the missing signal is genuinely higher order.
statements.gap: Canonne et al. characterize private tests for two simple product hypotheses using clamped one-record likelihood increments; their Section 3 construction does not apply when composite target fibers have intersecting one-record convex hulls.
statements.consumer: It rules out reverting to a randomized-treatment or additive one-record score for the full-fiber lift.

statements.statement: On every core \(C_j\), under every \(P_{s,\lambda}\), \(\mathbb E[Z_{12}\mid X_1,X_2\in C_j]=4sab\), independently of \(\lambda_j\). Hence \(\mathbb E_{P_{s,\lambda}^{\otimes n}}S_{\mathrm{pair}}=4sabkp_2\). For all replacement-neighboring datasets, \(|S_{\mathrm{pair}}(D_n)-S_{\mathrm{pair}}(D_n')|\le4\), so \(\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\le4\).
statements.justification: The nuisance sign disappears after two records collide, while realized occupancy normalization keeps sensitivity independent of nuisance dimension.
statements.gap: Chaudhuri et al. stabilize private U-statistics through local Hájek projections; this exact causal score instead exploits a shared-sign second moment within public cells.
statements.consumer: It supplies the signal and all-dataset privacy certificate for the sparse-occupancy pair test.

statements.statement: Suppose \(n\ge2\) and \(nv\le c_0\). The test \(\phi_{\mathrm{pair}}\) and estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) are pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially private under replacement adjacency. There are constants \(c,C>0\), independent of \(n,\epsilon,k,a,b\), such that \[\sup_{s\in\{-1,1\},\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^k}P_{s,\lambda}^{\otimes n}\{\phi_{\mathrm{pair}}\ne s\}\le C\exp(-ckp_2a^2b^2)+C\exp(-c\epsilon kp_2ab),\] and \[\sup_{s,\lambda}\mathbb E_{P_{s,\lambda}^{\otimes n}}|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{pair}}-\theta(P_{s,\lambda})|\le\frac{2ab}{1/4-a^2}\{C\exp(-ckp_2a^2b^2)+C\exp(-c\epsilon kp_2ab)\}.\] Neither bound contains \(\log k\) or \(\log|\{-1,1\}^k|\).
statements.justification: This is the higher-order escape: one explicit finite pure-private mechanism separates all nuisance profiles after one-record margins vanish.
statements.gap: Asi et al., Section 4.1, Theorem 13, Lemma 15, and Proposition 16 control generic finite covers through \(\log|\mathcal P_\eta|\); Bun et al., Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, similarly charge \(\log m\) or \(\log|\mathcal C_\alpha|\). The present structural pair test is not a generic improvement to those results, but its signed-family exponent requires no nuisance-catalogue selection.
statements.consumer: It provides the private upper-test counterpart for the shared-sign experiment that diagnoses the coupled \(r_F\) privacy branch.

statements.statement: In the specified experiment \((\mathcal Z_k^2,\overline\Pi_{s,k}^{\,2})\), \(\Pr(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{coll}})=1/k\) and \(\operatorname{TV}(\overline\Pi_{+,k}^{\,2},\overline\Pi_{-,k}^{\,2})=4ab/k\). With equal prior weights on \(s\), \(RR_{2,k}\) has Bayes classification error \(\{1-(4ab/k)\tanh(\epsilon/2)\}/2\), and \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{RR}}\) has Bayes absolute risk \[\frac{ab}{1/4-a^2}\{1-(4ab/k)\tanh(\epsilon/2)\}.\] For every adjacent pair under \(\sim_{\mathrm q}\), both output likelihood ratios are at most \(e^\epsilon\), and the maximum neighboring log-likelihood ratio is exactly \(\epsilon\).
statements.justification: The fully finite calculation separates the unavoidable collision loss from any nonexistent nuisance-entropy loss.
statements.gap: Generic cover bounds do not identify whether a loss in this experiment comes from collision probability or from the number of nuisance profiles.
statements.consumer: It supplies a reproducible, exact early-kill benchmark for the sample-level pair mechanism and its privacy constraints.

statements.statement: Under the two-scale geometric restriction \(q<\gamma\), \(a\asymp\ell^\alpha\), \(b\asymp\ell^\beta\), \(ab\asymp\delta\), \(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\), and \(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\), sparse occupancy gives \(kp_2\asymp n^2h^d\ell^d\). Thus the two exponents in Theorem 2 are bounded below by fixed positive constants when \(\delta\ge C\max\{r_{\mathrm{pair}},r_F\}\), and can be made arbitrarily large by increasing \(C\). This is a fixed-error pure-private separation guarantee, restricted to \(q<\gamma\) and \(nv\le c_0\), at the named coupled radius \(r_F=(n^2\epsilon)^{-1/D_F}\), without a nuisance-sign logarithm. For \(k=1\) and nuisance profile \(\lambda=(\lambda_1)\in\{-1,1\}\), let \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,X_i)\), \(i\in\{1,2\}\), be independent records from \(P_{s,(\lambda_1)}\), and set \(U_i=2A_i-1\), \(V_i=2Y_i-1\), and \(Z_{12}=(U_1V_2+V_1U_2)/2\). Then the sanity reduction is \[\mathbb E_{P_{s,(\lambda_1)}^{\otimes2}}\!\left[Z_{12}\,\middle|\,X_1,X_2\in C_1\right]=4sab.\]
statements.justification: The specialization makes the \(n^2\epsilon\) privacy balance explicit without importing a formula for full-class nonprivate risk.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. derive a nonprivate fuzzy-hypothesis rate, and Acharya et al. derive private mixture converses; neither constructs a private CATE test attaining this signed-family pair separation.
statements.consumer: It validates the \(r_F\) branch on the legal least-favorable experiment before any global target-fiber aggregation is attempted.

statements.statement: If every \(Q_t\) has replacement sensitivity at most one and \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le B\), then \(T_{\mathrm{shell}}\) is pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially private and \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}d_\Theta(T_{\mathrm{shell}},\theta(P))\le (B+3)r.\] The bound is independent of \(|\mathcal G_r|\) and of every nuisance-sieve cardinality.
statements.justification: This proposition turns the formerly informal shell requirement into the exact certificate needed for log-free scalar selection.
statements.gap: The exponential mechanism alone gives a global output-cardinality term; the displayed weighted expectation criterion replaces the global union bound with a summable distance-shell calculation.
statements.consumer: A full-class construction need only verify one-sensitivity and a uniform bound on \(\mathfrak W_r\) to obtain an \(O(r)\) estimator.

statements.statement: For every \(r\ge C\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},r_G,r_F\}\), can \(H_{\mathrm{pair\mbox{-}lift}}\) construct a family \(\{Q_t:t\in\mathcal G_r\}\) such that \(\sup_{D_n\sim_1D_n'}|Q_t(D_n)-Q_t(D_n')|\le1\) for every \(t\) and \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le C'\), with \(C'\) independent of every finite nuisance sieve, using the same sample size \(n\)?
statements.justification: This is the open step from the proved signed-family pair test to a symbolic full-class private upper frontier.
statements.gap: Birgé-style composite tests and Asi et al.'s Section 4 T-mechanism do not establish a nuisance-independent second-order projection certificate for arbitrary dependent least-favorable CATE mixtures.
statements.consumer: A positive answer and Proposition 3 yield \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\le C\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},r_G,r_F\}\); a negative answer identifies a privacy obstruction beyond the signed pair witness.

sampling_model.units: The records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent under each component law; each diagnostic sample mixture retains one shared nuisance-sign vector across all records.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with unknown Hölder propensity \(\pi\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator is supplied. The finite pair score averages out nuisance signs through an exact core-cell second moment and normalizes every occupied cell by its realized ordered-pair count.

target_estimand: \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(x_0)\), where \(\tau_P\) is the unique continuous Hölder representative of the conditional causal contrast

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 derive the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE minimax rate, and Section 5 develops the localized higher-order construction.
Section 3 constructs pure-private simple-hypothesis tests from clamped one-record log-likelihood ratios.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad lower bounds through mixture couplings and expected Hamming distance.
Section 4.1, Theorem 13, Lemma 15, and Proposition 16 give a pure-private T-mechanism whose generic finite-cover control contains \(\log|\mathcal P_\eta|\).
The paper constructs central-private U-statistic estimators using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 give pure-private finite-hypothesis and cover-based selection with costs proportional to \(\log m\) and \(\log|\mathcal C_\alpha|\).
The paper provides composition-based differentially private CATE meta-learners without a sharp pure-private pointwise Hölder minimax frontier.
Theorems 1 and 3 give observational Neyman-orthogonal CATE releases under approximate \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-differential privacy using Gaussian vector or Gaussian-process perturbations.

tldr: Unknown propensity can make separated pointwise CATE fibers have identical one-record nuisance mixtures while leaving an exact two-record signal. On a smooth signed family inside the unchanged exact-uniform Hölder class, an occupancy-normalized pair score removes the nuisance sign on every core, has replacement sensitivity at most four, and yields a finite pure-private test and two-point estimator with error \(C\exp(-ckp_2a^2b^2)+C\exp(-c\epsilon kp_2ab)\), without a nuisance-cardinality logarithm. A fully specified quantized experiment gives exact total-variation, Bayes-risk, and privacy calculations. Within the two-scale geometry \(q<\gamma\) and sparse-occupancy regime, the separation is \(\max\{r_{\mathrm{pair}},r_F\}\) on this signed experiment; the full-class frontier remains an open score-construction question stated through an explicit weighted shell functional.

project_justification.gap: Simple private tests use additive one-record likelihood increments, while generic private selection and T-mechanisms control finite covers through cardinality terms. The coupled CATE fibers here have intersecting one-record convex hulls, and the published results do not supply a nuisance-independent second-order score certificate for them.
project_justification.niche: A higher-order private test can use a signal common to every nuisance profile only when two observations occupy the same public localization cell. Realized occupancy normalization preserves constant replacement sensitivity and the \(n^2\epsilon\) pair-information balance.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs and audits the pair test on a legal smooth two-fiber family, proves an explicit pure-private test and risk bound, gives an exact finite experiment, and reduces the full-class lift to one precisely defined weighted shell functional.

related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024), Theorems 1--2 and Section 5, define the nonprivate Hölder pointwise-CATE benchmark and localized higher-order geometry; those results inform the smooth family but are not claimed as private comparators. Canonne et al. (2019), Section 3, construct optimal private simple tests from clamped one-record likelihood ratios; Theorem 1 identifies a composite-fiber convex-hull obstruction to that representation. Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021) provide central-private mixture converses through Hamming transport, informing the interpretation of the pair radius rather than its upper test. Asi et al. (2024), Section 4.1, Theorem 13, Lemma 15, and Proposition 16, control their pure-private T-mechanism over finite total-variation covers with \(\log|\mathcal P_\eta|\); the signed-family theorem avoids catalogue selection through a common pair orientation but does not claim a generic strengthening of their result. Bun et al. (2021), Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, give pure-private hypothesis and cover selection with \(\log m\) and \(\log|\mathcal C_\alpha|\) costs; those bounds are informed-by comparators rather than the same composite testing task. Chaudhuri et al. (2024) stabilize private U-statistics with local Hájek projections, while the exact core normalization and shared causal second moment here are problem-specific. Niu et al. (2022) give private CATE meta-learners without a pure-private pointwise Hölder frontier. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025), Theorems 1 and 3, give observational Neyman-orthogonal finite and functional CATE releases using Gaussian perturbations under approximate \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-privacy; they neither analyze pure privacy nor provide a shared-mixture pair test.
technical_internal_limitation: The early-kill experiment used \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\), \(n=2\), \(a=b=2/25\), and \(\epsilon=1\). For \(k=1,\ldots,8\), the finite nonprivate test and the pure-private linear program were solved on all \((4k)^2\) ordered datasets, with every one-record replacement edge imposed. The total variation was exactly \(0.0256/k\); the optimal private error equaled \(\{1-(0.0256/k)\tanh(1/2)\}/2\); randomized response attained that value; and the exhaustive maximum neighboring log-ratio was one. The exact symmetry formula was then checked through \(k=12\). The constant-mixture subexperiment verified convex-hull collision, while the shared-sign subexperiment verified the pair signal. The persistent loss was the collision probability \(1/k\), not a nuisance-entropy penalty. These finite checks do not prove the full-class lifting question, and the theorem deliberately remains in the sparse-occupancy regime \(nv\le c_0\); dense occupancy or arbitrary least-favorable priors may require a different concentration or stabilization argument.
honest_scope: The formal contribution is the exact-uniform smooth signed two-fiber family, its one-record convex-hull obstruction, the sparse-occupancy pure-private pair test, and a completely specified finite audit. The pair-radius specialization is restricted to the new two-scale geometry \(q<\gamma\) and \(nv\le c_0\); it makes no rate claim for \(q\ge\gamma\) or dense occupancy. It does not establish the full-class private minimax frontier. That frontier appears only as Open-ended Question 1 through a second-order least-favorable-mixture handle and the explicit functional \(\mathfrak W_r\). For \(k=1\) and \(\lambda=(\lambda_1)\), two independent records \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,X_i)\sim P_{s,(\lambda_1)}\), with \(U_i=2A_i-1\), \(V_i=2Y_i-1\), and \(Z_{12}=(U_1V_2+V_1U_2)/2\), obey \(\mathbb E_{P_{s,(\lambda_1)}^{\otimes2}}[Z_{12}\mid X_1,X_2\in C_1]=4sab\).
novelty_justification: The field-level novelty is a pure-private upper test on a legal causal family for which one-record nuisance mixtures coincide. The mechanism uses a bounded occupancy-normalized pair score with a common orientation over \(2^k\) profiles and obtains an error exponent independent of nuisance-catalogue size. Asi et al. and Bun et al. are treated as informed-by generic cover comparators, not as results globally tightened here. Schröder et al.'s approximate-private Gaussian CATE releases address a distinct privacy model and estimator architecture. The unresolved full-class projection certificate remains visible as an open question.
message: Recast q<gamma as an independently justified two-scale geometric restriction, stated the precise pair-radius regime, and replaced the undefined k=1 expectation with a fully specified component-law identity.
